title: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: submit, block and start automated investigations from advanced hunting
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the hunting actions, Plan 2 entitlement and the listed governance mechanisms, and the roadmap facts match the record. Minor corrections should complete two navigation paths, flag the beta role-assignment API and preserve qualifications about entry expiry and auditing defaults.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Analysts can submit false-positive or false-negative emails to Microsoft from advanced hunting query results.
claims.quote: **Submit to Microsoft** - select this action to submit false positive or false negative emails to Microsoft.

claims.claim: During submission, analysts can add URLs, URL domains, sender domains and file attachments to the Tenant Allow/Block List while Microsoft evaluates the submission.
claims.quote: As part of the submission, you can also add URLs and URL domains, sender domains, and file attachments to the Tenant Allow/Block List to immediately mitigate the reported false positive or false negative while Microsoft evaluates the submission.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Tenant Allow/Block List entries govern organisation-wide filtering rather than only the selected hunting-result mailbox.
claims.quote: Users in the organization can't send email to these blocked domains and addresses.

claims.claim: Allow entries skip filters associated with the allowed entity, but delivery still depends on other filtering checks.
claims.quote: During mail flow or time of click, if messages containing the entities in the allow entries pass other checks in the filtering stack, the messages are delivered (all filters associated with the allowed entities are skipped).

claims.claim: Block entries stop affected mail across the organisation.
claims.quote: Email messages that contain URL block entries are blocked as *high confidence phishing*. Messages containing URL block entries are quarantined.

**Approve**: Initiate the pending action.

claims.claim: Domain and email address, file and URL block entries expire after 30 days by default.
claims.quote: By default, the following types of block entries expire after 30 days, but you can set them to expire up to 90 days or to never expire:

claims.claim: Allow entries for these entity types are kept for 45 days after the filtering system determines the entity is clean.
claims.quote: By default, allow entries for domains and email addresses, files, and URLs are kept for 45 days after the filtering system determines that the entity is clean, and then the allow entry is removed.
claims.fix: Change the clause to 'and, by default, keeps allow entries for these entity types for 45 days after the filtering system determines that the entity is clean'. This is a configurable default, not an unconditional lifetime.

claims.claim: Outside the unified RBAC route, taking email actions through hunting requires a Defender for Office 365 role to search and purge emails.
claims.quote: To take action on emails through advanced hunting, you need a role in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 to search and purge emails.

claims.claim: Submit to Microsoft and Initiate automated investigation might be disabled when mandatory query-result columns are missing.
claims.quote: **Submit to Microsoft** might be disabled if mandatory columns are missing. ... **Initiate automated investigation** might be disabled if mandatory columns are missing.

claims.claim: Blocking URLs requires joining the URL information table.
claims.quote: To block a URL or URL domain, join the EmailUrlInfo table with NetworkMessageId to get the required details. To block an attachment (file), join the EmailAttachmentInfo table with NetworkMessageId to get the file's hash.

claims.claim: Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions > Security operations reaches the role-permission area in the Defender portal.
claims.quote: On the **Permissions** page, under **Microsoft Defender XDR**, select **Roles** > **Create custom role**. ... On the **Choose permissions** page ... **Security operations**
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles > Create custom role > Choose permissions > Security operations > Security data > Email & collaboration advanced actions (manage)' and retain the note to select Response (manage) in the same section. The final permission hierarchy is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-take-action.
